card.summary: The Disaster Assistance Simplification Act directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to create a single, unified intake process and system for people, businesses, and organizations applying for federal disaster assistance. The system aims to consolidate applications across multiple disaster assistance programs, allow applicants to check application statuses and update information, distribute recovery resources, and enable direct communication between agencies and survivors while meeting data security and privacy requirements.

summary: S. 1462, the Fix Our Forests Act, aims to improve forest management activities on National Forest System land, public land under the Bureau of Land Management, and Tribal land to reduce wildfire risks and return resilience to overgrown, fire-prone areas. The bill establishes programs, interagency centers, and streamlined procedures for hazardous fuels reduction, prescribed burning, reforestation, community protection, litigation reforms, and disaster assistance for wildland firefighters.

affected_groups.effect: Receive new casualty assistance programs, travel reimbursement for next-of-kin in cases of death or critical injury, and adjusted training requirements for supervisory roles.
Granted streamlined environmental reviews, new emergency management authority, expanded acreage limits for categorical exclusions, and mandated interagency reporting.
affected_groups.group: Federal Land Agencies (Forest Service, BLM, DOI)

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to enter shared stewardship agreements, participate in fireshed assessments, receive grants for prescribed burning and tree nurseries, and act as project sponsors.
Granted permission to remove trees within 150 feet of power lines, streamlined vegetation management plan review timelines, and timber cutting provisions without separate timber sales.
Impacted by the development of a targeted grazing strategy for wildfire risk reduction and potential temporary variances to grazing permits.

key_provisions: Establishes the Wildland Fire Intelligence Center and a public-facing Fireshed Registry to track wildfire exposure, hazardous fuels management activities, and environmental reviews.
Authorizes emergency fireshed management projects and amends the Healthy Forests Restoration Act to expand acreage caps for certain categorical exclusions from 3,000 to 10,000 acres.

Implements litigation reforms limiting preliminary and permanent injunctions, setting specific filing deadlines for claims, and establishing standards for judicial remand and vacatur regarding covered agency actions.
Expands prescribed fire activities, provides liability protections and training for non-Federal and Federal prescribed fire managers, and establishes smoke management coordination.
Creates the Community Wildfire Risk Reduction Program and a unified portal for disaster and wildfire defense grant applications.

Updates provisions for electric transmission and distribution facility rights-of-way, including hazard tree removal within 150 feet of power lines and automatic approval timelines for vegetation management plans.
Establishes the Wildland Fire Management Casualty Assistance Program to provide support and expense reimbursements to the next-of-kin of killed, critically injured, or ill firefighters.
missing_information: Specific funding authorization amounts and appropriations required to carry out the numerous newly established programs, centers, and grants.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 1462, the Fix Our Forests Act, aims to improve forest management activities on National Forest System land, public land under the Bureau of Land Management, and Tribal land to reduce wildfire risks and return resilience to overgrown, fire-prone areas. The bill establishes programs, interagency centers, and streamlined procedures for hazardous fuels reduction, prescribed burning, reforestation, community protection, litigation reforms, and disaster assistance for wildland firefighters.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping legislative effort to alter federal forest management, environmental review application, and wildfire mitigation across public and Tribal lands. By expanding expedited review authorities, altering judicial review standards, and creating interagency coordination centers, the legislation has a substantial impact on federal land management practices and the regulatory framework governing wildfire prevention.
